newsitem.title: PERU: U.S. group to sign contract for Peru oil block.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group to sign contract for Peru oil block.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Monday it would sign a contract Wednesday with a U.S. consortium of Barrett Resources Corporation and Advantage Resources Selva LLC for the rights to three oil blocks.

The contract, giving the group a license to explore and develop blocks 55A, 55B and 55C in the Peruvian jungle, is one of three contracts the state expects to sign this month with private oil companies, government daily El Peruano said.
These three contracts will involve a total initial investment of around $120 million.

El Peruano did not give more details about the other two contracts. It added, however, that the government was close to signing contracts with Peruvian miner Buenaventura, oil giants Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, and Argentina's Pluspetrol Corp.
The paper did not say if each of these companies would sign individual contracts or would form consortia for the oil block rights.
Each contract the government hopes to sign would involve an investment of around $40 million, El Peruano said.

The government has signed eight oil contracts so far this year. Energy and Mines Minister Alberto Pandolfi said last month Peru hoped to sign a further six contracts with private companies in the rest of 1996, and eight more in 1997.
The government currently has 33 contracts running, 18 for exploration and 15 for extraction.

A consortium of Shell and Mobil signed the most important of these contracts in May when it received the rights to appraise for two years the huge Camisea hydrocarbon reserves with a view to developing them.

If the oil consortium, in which Shell is the operating partner with a 57.5 percent share, decides to exploit the reserves, the project will last 40 years and become the largest foreign investment commitment in Peru at almost $3 billion.
